author: framework-coordinator
intent: Preserve the native veh_lift coordinate capture after optional map-bit handling and before record clearing, without changing stack or callback order.
evidence: The complete pinned span 005BFFA0..005C007E is decoded with match_recovery PeImage/Span and Capstone. 005C003A/0041 sign-extend the then-current x/y after the optional bit_set path; 005C004B stores VehDropLiftVehID; 005C0051..0066 clear x/y and both stack links; 005C0070/0076 publish the earlier x/y values to VehLiftX/Y.

The old source candidate read Vehs[veh_id].x/y only after setting the fields to -1, so it published (-1,-1) instead of the lifted unit's prior coordinates. The faithful source captures signed x/y after optional map-bit handling, before the drop-id store and field clears, and publishes them afterward. This preserves the original reload point relative to the optional bit_set call and all unsafe/error behavior.

The complete-body host fixture extracts Veh's actual signed int16 coordinate/link declarations and TerrainBit enum from their owners. It covers the linked-neighbor updates separately and together, a no-neighbor on-map bit_set branch checking its arguments/record state before mutation, and a no-neighbor off-map path. The old post-clear-read mutant removes capture locals and fails at the first coordinate assertion; a pre-bit_set capture mutant fails the synthetic coordinate-reload case. These controls do not assert that the real bit_set routine mutates vehicle records. Return-value checks retain the existing source behavior, with native 005C006D loading EDI into EAX before return.

No mapping, symbol, original marker, or historical TRIED note was removed or changed. The new concise source annotation explains that earlier matching candidate's post-clear reads contradicted native dataflow. No byte-exact, full-game, or runtime acceptance claim is made.
